vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: easy to reach, or easy to understand and enjoy
full of colour, energy and life
not as famous as it deserves to be
instantly recognised as the symbol of a place
small enough to walk across in a short time
real and traditional, not made for tourists
so big or intense that it is hard to take it all in
old but still in very good condition

paras: People always ask me which one is better, Dubrovnik or Ljubljana. After two weeks in both, I still cannot answer, because they are good at completely different things.

Dubrovnik is the more famous of the two, and it is easy to see why. The walls are the most iconic thing on the whole coast, and the old town is better preserved than almost any city I have visited. But it is also more crowded than I expected. In August the main street is overwhelming, and by eleven in the morning it is harder to walk than to stand still. Compared to that, the mornings are wonderful: at seven the stone is empty, quiet and completely yours.

Ljubljana is smaller, greener and much more compact. You can cross the centre on foot in twenty minutes, and the river is the best place in the city to do absolutely nothing. It is far less famous, so it is also far less expensive, and the food is more authentic than anything I ate on the coast. What makes it stand out is how relaxed it feels. It is not as dramatic as Dubrovnik, but it is more vibrant in the evening, and it is the most underrated capital in Europe. If you have ten days, do not choose. Take the slower road and see both.

listenings.text: People ask me every week which city they should choose, and I always give the same answer. If you have four days, go to Dubrovnik, because the walls are the most impressive thing on this coast and you should see them once in your life. But go in the morning. By noon the main street is more crowded than any place I know, and it becomes exhausting rather than beautiful. If you have ten days, add Ljubljana. It is quieter, greener and much cheaper, and honestly it is the most underrated capital in this part of Europe. The two cities are not competing. They are simply good at different things.

Welcome back to the tour. Look at the two buildings in front of you. The one on the left is older, but the one on the right is better preserved, and that is not an accident. The building on the right was restored twice, once after the earthquake and again in the nineteen nineties. The one on the left kept its original stone, so it is more authentic, but it is also far more fragile. Which is better? Architects argue about this everywhere in Europe. The most honest answer is that a city needs both: the building you restore, and the building you leave alone.

extra_audio.text: First she arrived in Dubrovnik and walked the walls at seven in the morning, when the stone was completely empty. By eleven the main street was more crowded than she expected, so she left the old town. Then she took the slower road north and arrived in Ljubljana in the evening. She crossed the whole centre on foot in twenty minutes and could not believe how compact it was. In the end she decided that the two cities are simply good at different things.
